title: Main idea of an informational passage
subtitle: Central Ideas and Details · 58 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **58 of the official questions in Central Ideas and Details are this one** — 17 Easy, 31 Medium, 10 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Medium tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The stem asks for the main idea of the text, or the text's main idea about a named person, and the passage is non-fiction: science, history, arts or social studies.
- Often the opening sentence gives a general claim or context and the later sentences give examples or a specific case.
- The four choices are full-sentence claims of similar length.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Before you look at the choices, say in a few words what the passage as a whole is building toward.
- That is often the claim the examples support, or the 'but' or 'however' turn.
- 2) Pick the choice that covers every sentence of the passage, not just one of them.
- 3) Check that the choice is no stronger or broader than the text: no 'always', no causes the text never states.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You pick a choice that repeats one vivid detail or example accurately but is only part of the point.
Or you pick one that stretches the topic into a claim the passage never makes, such as saying a new tool lets researchers do something bigger than what was actually described.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
